key_insight: A solver-agnostic PINN can learn turbulence closures that generalize across bluff-body shapes by enforcing the RANS equations directly during training.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening of closure forms and more transferable CFD models, with promising out-of-sample performance for drag and mean-flow prediction.
method: Train closures inside a PINN using automatic differentiation to impose the RANS residual without embedding a CFD solver.
Compare four closure types: three realizability-aware Reynolds-stress models and one direct Reynolds-force model.
Add input-gradient smoothing and a Lipschitz constraint to improve coupled stability before deploying the frozen closures in a finite-element solver.
evidence_signal: The closures were trained on six 2D bluff-body wakes at Re = 10^4 and evaluated with a strict leave-one-shape-out protocol; the force model achieved the best generalization, including about 8.5% LOSO drag error.
watch_item: Generalization depends on stable downstream deployment and the approach was demonstrated on 2D wakes, so extension to more complex 3D flows may require additional validation.
paper_title: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training
